name: Alemayehu Mekonen
tagline: I build backend systems that stay up — and the pipelines that keep them shipping.
bio: I'm a software engineer working across backend services, infrastructure and the delivery pipeline that connects them. Most of my work sits where those three meet: designing a service, containerising it, and making sure it can be deployed and observed without ceremony.

Today I work at Lion International Bank, where the systems I look after have low tolerance for downtime. That environment shapes how I build — I care more about a service that degrades predictably than one that is clever. Before this I built backend services at Safaricom Ethiopia with Spring Boot and Keycloak, and shipped full-stack products at Addis Software and Purpose Black Ethiopia.

I work mainly in Java and Spring Boot, TypeScript and Node.js, with Docker, Kubernetes and Jenkins for delivery. I'm most interested in the parts of a system that are hard to change later: service boundaries, authentication, and how failures propagate.

focusAreas.title: Backend engineering
focusAreas.description: Spring Boot and Node.js services, REST APIs, authentication with Keycloak and OAuth2, and message-driven communication with RabbitMQ.

focusAreas.title: Distributed systems
focusAreas.description: Decomposing applications into services with their own configuration, discovery, gateway and logging concerns — and keeping the seams between them explicit.

focusAreas.title: Delivery and operations
focusAreas.description: Jenkins pipelines, Docker images, Kubernetes workloads and Linux servers, with Grafana and Prometheus for visibility once it's running.

focusAreas.title: Full-stack product work
focusAreas.description: React and Next.js front-ends built against the APIs I design, so the contract between the two is deliberate rather than discovered.
